definition: Fraction of training groups in which all G=4 sampled rollouts received identical rewards. When reward standard deviation within a group is zero, the GRPO advantage A_i = (R_i - mean(R)) / std(R) is zero for every rollout, so that group contributes no gradient. The model learns nothing from that problem.
why_it_matters: This is the core mechanistic claim of TAPR. It is measured directly by the trainer, not inferred. Outcome-only GRPO is blind on a majority of its training data; TAPR restores signal on nearly all of it.
provenance: exact — logged by GRPOTrainer every 10 steps, transcribed from Colab run logs

tapr.note: Reaches ~0 within the first few steps and stays there.

strategyqa.note: StrategyQA baseline degeneracy (~0.625) exceeds GSM8K baseline degeneracy (~0.525). Hypothesis: on a binary yes/no task, an uncertain model tends to emit the same answer across all four rollouts, collapsing reward variance more often than on numeric-answer tasks.

smoke_test_confirmation.note: Judge returned a real score (0.74), not the 0.5 parse-failure fallback, confirming the scoring path was live and correct before the full run.

interpretation.claim: TAPR eliminates reward degeneracy. This is causal and definitional, not correlational — if within-group reward variance is zero, the advantage is mathematically zero.
interpretation.consistency: The same pattern holds across two structurally different tasks (numeric-answer math and binary yes/no reasoning), suggesting the mechanism is task-agnostic.
interpretation.connection_to_transfer: The proposed link to the cross-task transfer result: ORM trains on ~47% of its data and over-fits to a narrow format; TAPR trains on ~100% and learns a broader policy. This link is a hypothesis, not yet established — the policy drift experiment is designed to test it.
